mainTopic: The language of קריאת שמע (רבי vs. רבנן), and the source and reasons for the fixed order of the blessings of שמונה עשרה.
overview: This amud finishes the מחלוקת about the language of קריאת שמע. רבי learns from ״וְהָיוּ״ that שמע must be said in לשון הקודש, and רבנן learn from ״שְׁמַע״ that any language you understand is allowed. Each side then explains its use of the other side's word. For רבי, ״שְׁמַע״ teaches השמע לאזניך. For רבנן, ״וְהָיוּ״ teaches not to read למפרע, and רבי learns that rule from ״הַדְּבָרִים״ instead. The גמרא tries to learn each side's view about reading the whole Torah in other languages, and rejects both attempts. Then it turns to תפלה: the eighteen blessings were set ״עַל הַסֵּדֶר״, by שמעון הפקולי and by the 120 elders. A long ברייתא then explains, mostly from פסוקים, why each blessing of שמונה עשרה stands where it does, from אבות through בונה ירושלים. The amud ends as it begins the reason that את צמח דוד follows, and that reason continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי's source: the word ״וְהָיוּ״ means the words stay as they are
steps.stepSummary: רבי learns from ״וְהָיוּ״ that the words of שמע must stay in their original form, meaning לשון הקודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And they shall be": they must stay just as they are.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for רבי's view that שמע must be said in לשון הקודש. ״וְהָיוּ״ is read as 'they shall stay in their original state.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous amud, the גמרא asked why רבי requires לשון הקודש. The answer is that ״וְהָיוּ הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה״ means these words must remain as they were written, in Hebrew. Translating them would change their form.

keyTerms.meaning: In their original state, as they are

steps.confusionAlert: ״וְהָיוּ״ is not being read as a simple 'and they will be.' The דרשה hears 'as they are' in it, meaning the words must stay unchanged.

phrases.english: "And they shall be": in their original state they shall be.
phrases.notes: This finishes רבי's reason, which began in the previous section.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question 'what is רבי's reason?', which was asked on the previous amud.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי learns from ״וְהָיוּ״ that שמע must stay in its original language.

steps.title: What is רבנן's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבנן, who allow שמע in any language.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבנן, what is their reason?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know רבי's source, the גמרא asks where רבנן get their view. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides of a מחלוקת need a source in the פסוק. רבנן, who allow any language, also need a word in the Torah to rely on.

phrases.english: And the Sages, what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי's source to asking for רבנן's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that shows שמע may be said in any language.

steps.title: רבנן's source: ״שְׁמַע״ means hear in any language you understand
steps.stepSummary: רבנן learn from ״שְׁמַע״, read as 'understand,' that שמע may be said in any language a person understands.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says "Hear": in any language that you hear (understand).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבנן read ״שְׁמַע״ as 'understand.' So you may say שמע in any language you understand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שמע can mean 'hear' or 'understand.' רבנן take it to mean the goal is understanding, so the language does not matter.

phrases.english: The verse says: "Hear,"
in any language that you hear (understand).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי: ״וְהָיוּ״ means only לשון הקודש. רבנן: ״שְׁמַע״ means any language you understand.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי also has the word 'שמע'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי does with ״שְׁמַע״, since it is written in the Torah for him too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רבי too, isn't "Hear" written?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי: the word ״שְׁמַע״ is in the Torah, so what does he learn from it, if not 'any language'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the Torah must teach something. If רבי does not use ״שְׁמַע״ to permit any language, he needs a different use for it.

phrases.english: And Rebbi too, isn't it written: "Hear"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבנן's source into a question against רבי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's view that שמע must be in לשון הקודש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word ״שְׁמַע״ seems to teach 'any language.' What does רבי do with it?

steps.title: רבי uses 'שמע' to require saying it audibly
steps.stepSummary: For רבי, ״שְׁמַע״ teaches השמע לאזניך: you must say שמע loud enough to hear your own words.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word is needed to teach: let your ears hear what your mouth says.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי uses ״שְׁמַע״ for a different rule: you must say שמע loud enough to hear yourself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי reads ״שְׁמַע״ in its plain sense of physical hearing. That rule uses up the word, so it is not free to teach 'any language.'

keyTerms.meaning: What you bring out of your mouth (say)

phrases.english: That (word) he needs for:
Make heard to your ears
what you bring out of your mouth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the word to a different דרשה

steps.title: רבנן hold you are יוצא even without hearing yourself
steps.stepSummary: רבנן do not need ״שְׁמַע״ for השמע לאזניך, because they hold that someone who did not hear his own words is still יצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבנן hold like the one who said: one who reads שמע but did not make his ears hear it has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבנן avoid the rule רבי learned. They hold that hearing yourself is not required to be יצא, so ״שְׁמַע״ is free for 'any language.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The unspoken question is: where do רבנן learn השמע לאזניך? The answer is that they do not hold it is required. They follow the view that you are יצא even if you did not hear yourself.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold like the one who said
Made it heard to his ears

steps.confusionAlert: רבנן do not say that whispering silently is ideal. They only say that after the fact you are יצא. This is the first, unattributed opinion (תנא קמא) in the משנה in ברכות (טו.). רבי יוסי there disagrees and says you are not יצא.

phrases.english: And the Sages hold like the one who said:
one who reads the Shema
and did not make it heard to his ear has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבנן do not need ״שְׁמַע״ for the rule רבי learned from it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ties רבנן to an existing opinion about the law
steps.terutzMaskana: רבנן hold that hearing yourself is not required, so ״שְׁמַע״ teaches 'any language.'

steps.title: Challenge: רבנן also have the word ״וְהָיוּ״
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא turns to רבנן: what do they do with ״וְהָיוּ״?
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רבנן too, isn't "And they shall be" written?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the mirror image of step 4. The גמרא asks what רבנן learn from ״וְהָיוּ״, if not 'only לשון הקודש.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן ignore רבי's reading of ״וְהָיוּ״. They still need some teaching from this word.

phrases.english: And the Sages too, isn't it written "And they shall be"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבי's source into a question against רבנן, matching step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבנן's view that any language is allowed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word ״וְהָיוּ״ seems to require the original language. What do רבנן do with it?

steps.title: רבנן use ״וְהָיוּ״ to forbid reading out of order
steps.stepSummary: For רבנן, ״וְהָיוּ״ teaches that שמע may not be said למפרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word is needed to teach that one may not read it out of order.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבנן read ״וְהָיוּ״ as 'they must stay as they are' in their order, not their language.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that ״וְהָיוּ״ means 'as they are.' They argue about what must stay the same. רבי says the language; רבנן say the order of the words.

phrases.english: That (word) they need
that one should not read out of order.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ שֶׁלֹּא יִקְרָא לְמַפְרֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the word to a different דרשה

steps.title: Where does רבי learn the rule against reading out of order?
steps.stepSummary: רבי used ״וְהָיוּ״ for language, so where does he get the rule against reading למפרע?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי, from where does he learn that one may not read out of order?
steps.whatsHappening: Everyone agrees שמע may not be said out of order. Since רבי used ״וְהָיוּ״ for language, the גמרא asks for his source for this rule. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule against למפרע is accepted by all. Each side must therefore have a source for it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it?

phrases.english: And Rebbi, that one should not read out of order,
from where does he know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי, שֶׁלֹּא יִקְרָא לְמַפְרֵעַ מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 8: the rule needs a source in רבי's view too.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי's source for not reading שמע למפרע.

steps.title: רבי learns it from 'the words' instead of 'words'
steps.stepSummary: רבי learns the rule against reading למפרע from the extra ה in ״הַדְּבָרִים״.
steps.simpleTranslation: From "words" versus "the words."
steps.whatsHappening: The answer: the פסוק says ״הַדְּבָרִים״ ('THE words') and not just 'words.' This points to the specific words in their set order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra ה makes the words definite, meaning these exact words in this exact order. So רבי does not need ״וְהָיוּ״ for this rule.

phrases.english: From "words" versus "the words."
phrases.notes: The extra ה ('the') is the key: that one little letter is what we learn from here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra ה in ״הַדְּבָרִים״ teaches the fixed order.

steps.title: רבנן do not expound the extra 'the'
steps.stepSummary: רבנן do not learn anything from the difference between 'words' and 'the words.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבנן: "words" versus "the words" means nothing to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבנן cannot use רבי's source for the order rule. For them, the extra ה teaches nothing, so they need ״וְהָיוּ״ for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the circle. Each side's way of reading the פסוקים is consistent. On the למפרע rule, the difference is whether the ה in ״הַדְּבָרִים״ teaches something; the core disagreement remains the language of שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: It does not mean anything to them

steps.whatToRemember: רבי: ״וְהָיוּ״ means לשון הקודש; ״שְׁמַע״ means השמע לאזניך; ״הַדְּבָרִים״ means not למפרע. רבנן: ״שְׁמַע״ means any language; ״וְהָיוּ״ means not למפרע; they do not expound the ה, and they hold you are יצא without hearing yourself.

phrases.english: And the Sages: "words" versus "the words"
does not teach anything to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבנן do not adopt רבי's source from step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבנן do not expound the extra ה, so they need ״וְהָיוּ״ for the order rule.

steps.title: Proposal: does רבי hold the whole Torah may be read in any language?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests with לימא that רבי holds the whole Torah may be said in any language. Otherwise, why would he need ״וְהָיוּ״ to require Hebrew for שמע?
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רבי holds the entire Torah may be said in any language? For if you think it may only be said in the holy tongue, why do I need the Torah to write "And they shall be"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a possible conclusion from רבי's view. This is a proposal that sets up the next move, and the next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the whole Torah already had to be in לשון הקודש, there would be no need for a special פסוק about שמע. Since רבי needs ״וְהָיוּ״, it seems that for him the rest of the Torah may be said in any language. A לימא is often rejected later, so this is not yet a conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: It enters your mind, you might think

steps.confusionAlert: Do not treat the לימא as the final answer. It is only a suggestion that the גמרא is about to examine.
steps.whyThisMatters: This question widens the discussion from שמע to the status of the whole Torah in translation, which matters for the laws of reading in other languages.

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rebbi holds
that the entire Torah, all of it,
may be said in any language?
For if it enters your mind
that it may be said only in the holy tongue,
why do I need it to write "And they shall be"!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא קָסָבַר רַבִּי כׇּל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ בְּכׇל לָשׁוֹן נֶאֶמְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both sides' sources are settled, the גמרא draws a wider inference from רבי's need for ״וְהָיוּ״.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי holds that the rest of the Torah may be said in any language, since he needed a special פסוק for שמע.

steps.title: רבי needed וְהָיוּ to block a mistaken reading of שְׁמַע
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion that רבי holds the whole Torah may be read in any language is rejected. Even if the Torah generally must be read in Hebrew, the verse was still needed for שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary. You might have thought that 'שְׁמַע' means 'understand,' like רבנן say. So the Torah wrote 'וְהָיוּ.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the לימא from step 12. רבי could still hold that the Torah must be read in Hebrew, and he still needs ״וְהָיוּ״ for שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 argued that if the whole Torah must be in Hebrew anyway, רבי would not need a special verse for שמע. The answer is that the word ״שְׁמַע״ (understand) could have made us think שמע is an exception that may be said in any language. ״וְהָיוּ״ blocks that idea and keeps שמע in Hebrew.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary (the verse was still needed)
It would have entered your mind (you might have thought)

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not prove what רבי actually holds about the rest of the Torah. It only shows that the proof from step 12 does not work.

phrases.english: It was necessary,
phrases.notes: The verse ״וְהָיוּ״ was still needed, even for רבי.

phrases.english: you might have thought 'hear' means understand, like the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: If ״שְׁמַע״ means 'understand,' then any language would work.

phrases.english: so the Merciful One wrote 'and they shall be.'
phrases.notes: This teaches that שמע must be said in Hebrew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the לימא inference about רבי from step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רבי must hold the whole Torah may be read in any language.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The verse ״וְהָיוּ״ had a separate purpose: to stop us from reading ״שְׁמַע״ as permission for any language.

steps.title: Do רבנן hold the whole Torah must be read in Hebrew?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries the same move on רבנן. If the whole Torah may be read in any language, they would not need ״שְׁמַע״ to permit שמע in any language.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that the רבנן hold the whole Torah must be said in the holy language? Because if you think it may be said in any language, why do I need the Torah to write 'שְׁמַע'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now suggests the opposite inference about רבנן. Since they need ״שְׁמַע״ to allow any language, maybe the rest of the Torah must be in Hebrew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors step 12. רבנן use ״שְׁמַע״ to teach that שמע may be said in any language. That verse would seem extra if the whole Torah were already allowed in any language, so the גמרא suggests רבנן hold that the Torah in general must be in Hebrew.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (the verse seems extra)

phrases.english: Shall we say the Rabbis hold
phrases.notes: The גמרא is just trying out this idea here; it's not the final answer.

phrases.english: that the entire Torah must be said in the holy language,
because if you think
it may be said in any language,
why do I need the Torah to write 'hear'!
phrases.notes: Why would שמע need a special verse to permit any language?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 12, now applied to רבנן instead of רבי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבנן hold that the Torah in general must be read in Hebrew, based on their need for ״שְׁמַע״.

steps.title: רבנן needed שְׁמַע to block a mistaken reading of וְהָיוּ
steps.stepSummary: The inference about רבנן is rejected. Without ״שְׁמַע״, one might have read ״וְהָיוּ״ like רבי and required Hebrew.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary. You might have said that 'וְהָיוּ' teaches Hebrew, like רבי says. So the Torah wrote 'שְׁמַע.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 14. רבנן could hold that the whole Torah may be read in any language, and they still need ״שְׁמַע״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without ״שְׁמַע״, we might have learned from ״וְהָיוּ״ (as רבי does) that שמע is an exception that must be said in Hebrew. ״שְׁמַע״ (understand) tells us שמע is not an exception, so any language works. So neither side's view on the whole Torah can be proven from this מחלוקת.
steps.whatToRemember: The מחלוקת between רבי and רבנן about שמע does not tell us their view on reading the rest of the Torah. Each side's verse was needed to block a mistaken reading of the other verse.

phrases.english: It was necessary,
you might have said 'and they shall be' teaches Hebrew, like Rabbi,
so the Merciful One wrote 'hear.'
phrases.notes: This teaches that שמע may be said in any language you understand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the לימא about רבנן from step 14, mirroring step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רבנן must hold the whole Torah must be read in Hebrew.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The verse ״שְׁמַע״ was needed to stop us from reading ״וְהָיוּ״ as a Hebrew requirement.

steps.title: What is the source that תפלה must be said in order?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to תפלה, which the earlier ברייתא listed among things that may not be said out of order, and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: תפלה — from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It sets up the next step by asking how we know the blessings of תפלה must be said in their set order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already found the source for שמע not being said למפרע (״וְהָיוּ״ or the extra ה). The earlier ברייתא also included תפלה in that rule, so now the גמרא needs a source for תפלה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: Prayer — from where do we know this?
phrases.notes: The question is how we know prayer may not be said out of order.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the language discussion and returns to the list of things not said למפרע.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the blessings of תפלה have a fixed order that may not be changed.

steps.title: שמעון הפקולי arranged the eighteen blessings in order
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that שמעון הפקולי arranged the eighteen blessings in order before רבן גמליאל in יבנה. This shows the order is fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: שמעון הפקולי arranged the eighteen blessings before רבן גמליאל, in order, in יבנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא. Because the blessings were set up in a specific order, that order may not be changed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key words are ״עַל הַסֵּדֶר״ (in order). The blessings were not just written; they were arranged in a set sequence. So saying them out of order breaks that arrangement.

keyTerms.meaning: The eighteen blessings of the עמידה

phrases.english: As it is taught:
Shimon HaPakuli arranged
the eighteen blessings
before Rabban Gamliel
in order, in Yavne.
phrases.notes: ״עַל הַסֵּדֶר״ is the source that the order is fixed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The blessings were arranged ״עַל הַסֵּדֶר″ by שמעון הפקולי, so their order is fixed.

steps.title: The 120 elders set the eighteen blessings in order
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן (or a ברייתא) teaches that 120 elders, including several prophets, established the eighteen blessings in order. This is another source for the fixed order.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said, and some say a ברייתא taught: 120 elders, and among them several prophets, established the eighteen blessings in order.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source that the blessings were set in a fixed order. This time the order goes back to the אנשי כנסת הגדולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This source adds that the order was set by a great court that included prophets, which gives it even more authority. It also raises a puzzle, since the previous step said שמעון הפקולי arranged them. The גמרא takes up that puzzle on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא (a teaching from the תנאים)

steps.whyThisMatters: Both sources say the blessings were set ״עַל הַסֵּדֶר״. That is the basis for the rule that the עמידה may not be said out of order.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said,
and some say it was taught in a baraita:
A hundred and twenty elders,
and among them several prophets,

phrases.aramaic: תִּיקְּנוּ שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה בְּרָכוֹת עַל הַסֵּדֶר.
phrases.english: established the eighteen blessings in order.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source for the fixed order, and it seems to conflict with the attribution to שמעון הפקולי.
steps.raayaObject: That the eighteen blessings have a fixed order.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement of רבי יוחנן (or a ברייתא) about the 120 elders.

steps.title: Sources for the first three blessings
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא derives the blessings of אבות, גבורות and קדושות, in that order, from consecutive פסוקים in תהלים כט.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: From where do we know to say the blessing of the Fathers? Because it says, 'Give to ה׳, sons of the mighty.' From where do we know to then say the blessing of mighty deeds? Because it says, 'Give to ה׳ glory and strength.' From where do we know to then say the blessing of holiness? Because it says, 'Give to ה׳ the glory of His name, bow to ה׳ in the beauty of holiness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that starts explaining the order of the שמונה עשרה, beginning with the first three blessings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each blessing is matched to a phrase in תהלים כט, in the same order the phrases appear. 'בני אלים' (sons of the mighty) refers to the אבות, the great people of the world. 'כבוד ועוז' (glory and strength) matches גבורות, and 'הדרת קדש' (beauty of holiness) matches קדושת השם.

keyTerms.meaning: The first blessing of the עמידה, about אברהם, יצחק and יעקב
The second blessing, about ה׳'s mighty deeds (such as reviving the dead)
The third blessing, about ה׳'s holiness
'Sons of the mighty', read here as the אבות

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens the full explanation of why each blessing of the עמידה sits exactly where it does. It builds on the earlier point that the order was fixed by the Sages.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
From where do we know that we say the blessing of the Fathers?
As it says: 'Give to ה׳, sons of the mighty.'
phrases.notes: תהלים כט:א. The 'mighty ones' are the אבות.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that we say the blessing of mighty deeds?
As it says: 'Give to ה׳ glory and strength.'
And from where do we know that we say the blessing of holiness?
As it says: 'Give to ה׳ the glory of His name,'
phrases.notes: תהלים כט:ב

phrases.english: 'bow to ה׳ in the beauty of holiness.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having shown that the order is fixed, the גמרא now gives the reasons for that order, one blessing at a time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The order אבות, גבורות, קדושות follows the order of the phrases in תהלים כט:א-ב.

steps.title: Why understanding comes after holiness
steps.stepSummary: בינה follows קדושה because in ישעיה כט a verse about sanctifying ה׳ is followed right away by a verse about gaining understanding.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did they choose to say the blessing of understanding after the blessing of holiness? Because it says, 'They shall sanctify the Holy One of יעקב and revere the God of Israel,' and right next to it, 'Those who strayed in spirit will know understanding.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and explains why the fourth blessing, בינה (understanding), comes right after the blessing of holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works from two verses that sit side by side. The verse about holiness (ישעיה כט:כג) is followed directly by the verse about understanding (ישעיה כט:כד), so the blessings follow the same order.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What did they see' — why did the Sages choose this order?
'And next to it' — the following verse sits right beside it

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה רָאוּ לוֹמַר בִּינָה אַחַר קְדוּשָּׁה —
phrases.english: And why did they choose to say understanding after holiness?
As it says: 'They shall sanctify the Holy One of Yaakov'
phrases.notes: ישעיה כט:כג

phrases.english: 'and revere the God of Israel,'
and right next to it:
'Those who strayed in spirit will know understanding.'
phrases.notes: ישעיה כט:כד

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה רָאוּ לוֹמַר בִּינָה אַחַר קְדוּשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's explanation of the order with the next blessing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בינה comes after קדושה because the verses about them sit side by side in ישעיה כט.

steps.title: Why repentance comes after understanding
steps.stepSummary: תשובה follows בינה because a פסוק says 'his heart will understand, and he will return.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did they choose to say the blessing of repentance after understanding? Because it is written, 'His heart will understand, and he will return and be healed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains why the fifth blessing, תשובה (repentance), comes after בינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ישעיה ו:י, understanding ('יבין') comes first and returning ('ושב') follows, so the blessings follow the same order. But notice that the same verse ends with 'and be healed' — the next steps will be built on that.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה רָאוּ לוֹמַר תְּשׁוּבָה אַחַר בִּינָה —
phrases.english: And why did they choose to say repentance after understanding?
As it is written: 'His heart will understand, and he will return and be healed.'
phrases.notes: ישעיה ו:י

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה רָאוּ לוֹמַר תְּשׁוּבָה אַחַר בִּינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the chain of the order with the next blessing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תשובה comes after בינה because of the sequence 'יבין ושב' in the verse.

steps.title: Then healing should come after repentance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the order: the same verse continues 'and be healed,' so רפואה should come right after תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let us say the blessing of healing right after repentance!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the order using the very verse just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we follow the order of the words in 'יבין ושב ורפא לו,' then after 'returning' comes 'healing.' Yet in the עמידה, the blessing after תשובה is סליחה (forgiveness), not רפואה. So the verse seems to point to a different order.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If so' — if we follow your logic

phrases.english: If so,
let us say healing right after repentance?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי — לֵימָא רְפוּאָה בָּתְרַהּ דִּתְשׁוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the proof verse of step 21 against the actual order of the blessings.
steps.kashyaTarget: The placement of סליחה (rather than רפואה) right after תשובה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same verse that puts תשובה after בינה continues with 'ורפא לו,' which suggests רפואה should come next.

steps.title: A different verse puts forgiveness after repentance
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in ישעיה נה puts returning to ה׳ right before His great forgiveness, so סליחה follows תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't think that! For it is written: 'Let him return to ה׳ and He will have mercy on him, and to our God, for He will greatly forgive.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that another verse links repentance directly to forgiveness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ישעיה נה:ז, returning ('וישוב') is followed by ה׳'s mercy and great forgiveness ('ירבה לסלוח'). This verse supports placing סליחה right after תשובה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It cannot enter your mind' — that idea is rejected

phrases.english: It cannot enter your mind,
as it is written: 'Let him return to ה׳ and He will have mercy on him,'
phrases.notes: ישעיה נה:ז

phrases.english: 'and to our God, for He will greatly forgive.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, דִּכְתִיב: ״וְיָשׁוֹב אֶל ה׳ וִירַחֲמֵהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22 by bringing a verse that supports the actual order.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of 'ושב ורפא לו,' רפואה should follow תשובה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of 'וישוב אל ה׳... כי ירבה לסלוח,' סליחה follows תשובה.

steps.title: Why rely on this verse and not the other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we should follow the forgiveness verse instead of the healing verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see to rely on this verse? Rely on that one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer: there are now two verses pointing in two directions, so why prefer the forgiveness verse?
steps.deeperAnalysis: One verse puts healing after returning, and the other puts forgiveness after returning. Nothing so far explains why the forgiveness verse should win.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What did you see?' — why choose this option over the other?

phrases.english: And what did you see to rely on this one?
Rely on that one!
phrases.notes: That is, on 'ושב ורפא לו.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי חָזֵית דְּסָמְכַתְּ אַהָא? סְמוֹךְ אַהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 23 as an arbitrary choice between two verses.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of ישעיה נה:ז over ישעיה ו:י
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two verses point in different directions, so choosing one needs a reason.

steps.title: A third verse puts healing after forgiveness
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in תהלים קג lists forgiveness, then healing, then redemption, which breaks the tie in favor of סליחה before רפואה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another verse is written: 'Who forgives all your sins, who heals all your illnesses, who redeems your life from the pit.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third verse that breaks the tie.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In תהלים קג:ג-ד, forgiveness comes first and healing comes after it. So healing belongs after forgiveness, not directly after repentance.

phrases.english: Another verse is written:
'Who forgives all your sins,'
phrases.notes: תהלים קג:ג

phrases.english: 'who heals all your illnesses,'
'who redeems your life from the pit.'
phrases.notes: תהלים קג:ד

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24 by bringing a third verse that settles which order is right.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two verses are equally strong, so the choice seems arbitrary.
steps.terutzMaskana: תהלים קג clearly puts healing after forgiveness, which supports סליחה coming first.

steps.title: But the verse still says 'return and be healed'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא presses: if healing and redemption come after forgiveness, what do we do with 'ושב ורפא לו,' which puts healing right after returning?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that redemption and healing come after forgiveness? But it is written: 'He will return and be healed'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: the first verse is still there and still seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even with the third verse, ישעיה ו:י still says healing comes right after returning. So the verses still seem to clash, and the clash needs to be resolved.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But isn't it written...?' — opens a contradiction from a verse

phrases.aramaic: לְמֵימְרָא דִּגְאוּלָּה וּרְפוּאָה בָּתַר סְלִיחָה הִיא,
phrases.english: Is that to say that redemption and healing come after forgiveness?
But it is written: 'He will return and be healed'!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דִּגְאוּלָּה וּרְפוּאָה בָּתַר סְלִיחָה הִיא, וְהָכְתִיב: ״וָשָׁב וְרָפָא לוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 25 by setting it against the verse from step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that healing comes after forgiveness
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ישעיה ו:י still puts healing directly after repentance, which contradicts תהלים קג.

steps.title: That 'healing' means forgiveness
steps.stepSummary: The 'healing' in 'ושב ורפא לו' is not healing from illness. It is the spiritual healing of forgiveness, so that verse also supports סליחה after תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is not talking about healing from illnesses. It is talking about the healing of forgiveness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the clash by reading 'healing' in ישעיה as a word for forgiveness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once 'ורפא לו' is read as 'he will be forgiven,' the verses no longer clash. ישעיה ו:י now also says that forgiveness follows repentance, and תהלים קג puts physical healing after forgiveness. So the order תשובה, סליחה, then רפואה stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'healing' of forgiveness, meaning spiritual healing
Healing from illness, meaning physical healing

steps.whatToRemember: The order of the opening blessings comes from פסוקים: אבות, גבורות, קדושה (from תהלים כט), then בינה, then תשובה (from ישעיה). סליחה comes next, not רפואה, because the 'healing' in 'ושב ורפא לו' means forgiveness.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'ורפא לו' as physical healing here. The whole answer depends on understanding it as forgiveness.

phrases.english: That one is not healing from illnesses,
but rather the healing of forgiveness.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא לָאו רְפוּאָה דְתַחְלוּאִים הִיא, אֶלָּא רְפוּאָה דִסְלִיחָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 26 and closes the challenge first raised in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a word in the verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ורפא לו' means physical healing, so רפואה should follow תשובה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ורפא לו' means forgiveness, so סליחה follows תשובה and physical רפואה comes after סליחה.

steps.title: Why is redemption the seventh blessing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברכה of גאולה was placed seventh in שמונה עשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did they choose to put the blessing of redemption seventh?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next ברכה in the order and asks why גאולה sits in the seventh spot. This sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the order was explained by which idea logically follows which. Here the question is about the actual number, 'seventh,' so the answer will need to explain why the number seven fits גאולה.

keyTerms.meaning: What did they see / why did they decide (asking for the reason behind an arrangement)

phrases.english: And what did they see to say
redemption as the seventh?
phrases.notes: The seventh ברכה of the עמידה is 'ראה בעניינו… גואל ישראל'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the order of תשובה, סליחה and רפואה to the placement of the next ברכה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason גאולה is placed specifically as the seventh ברכה.

steps.title: רבא: the redemption will come in the seventh year
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that since Israel is destined to be redeemed in the seventh year of the שמיטה cycle, the ברכה of גאולה was put seventh.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: since they are destined to be redeemed in the seventh year, they set it as the seventh blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers that the number seven matches גאולה because the final redemption is expected in the seventh year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא links the place in the תפילה to a tradition about when the redemption will happen. The ברכה's number mirrors the year of the redemption: seventh blessing, seventh year.

keyTerms.meaning: They established it / fixed it in place

steps.confusionAlert: 'שביעית' does double duty here. The ברכה is seventh in the עמידה, and the redemption comes in the seventh year of the seven-year שמיטה cycle.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Since they are destined to be redeemed in the seventh [year],
phrases.notes: The seventh year of the שמיטה cycle.

phrases.english: therefore they fixed it as the seventh [blessing].

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁעֲתִידִין לִיגָּאֵל בִּשְׁבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: גאולה is seventh because the redemption is destined to come in the seventh year of the שמיטה cycle.

steps.title: Challenge: משיח comes only after the seventh year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: in the sixth year there are sounds, in the seventh wars, and after the seventh בן דוד comes. So the redemption is not in the seventh year.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't the Master say: in the sixth year there will be sounds, in the seventh wars, and at the end of the seventh בן דוד comes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's answer with a ברייתא saying משיח arrives only after the seventh year ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's reason depends on the redemption happening during the seventh year. The ברייתא puts the arrival of בן דוד in מוצאי שביעית, the year after. If that is right, the number seven seems not to fit גאולה.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't the Master say (introduces a contradicting source)
The end of the seventh year, meaning the year after it
The son of David, the משיח

phrases.english: But didn't the Master say:
in the sixth [year], sounds;
in the seventh, wars;
at the conclusion of the seventh, the son of David comes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer from step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the redemption happens in the seventh year.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא places the coming of משיח after the seventh year, so the seventh year is not the year of redemption.

steps.title: The wars are already the start of redemption
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the war of the seventh year is itself the beginning of the redemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: War is also the beginning of the redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא: the redemption process already begins with the wars of the seventh year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer widens what counts as 'redemption.' It is not only the moment משיח arrives but a process, and the seventh-year wars are its first stage. So it is still accurate to say Israel is redeemed in the seventh year.
steps.whatToRemember: גאולה is the seventh ברכה because the redemption begins in the seventh year with its wars, even though משיח himself comes afterward.

phrases.english: War, too,
is the beginning of redemption.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 30 and keeps רבא's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition: redemption is a process that begins with the wars.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Redemption means only the arrival of בן דוד, which happens after the seventh year.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wars of the seventh year are already part of the redemption, so the seventh year fits.

steps.title: Why is healing the eighth blessing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רפואה was placed as the eighth ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did they choose to put healing eighth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next ברכה and asks why רפואה is in the eighth spot. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא explained why רפואה comes after סליחה by the meaning of the ideas. Now it asks for a reason tied to the number eight itself.

phrases.english: And what did they see to say
healing as the eighth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same question pattern as step 28, applied to the next ברכה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason רפואה is specifically the eighth ברכה.

steps.title: רבי אחא: מילה on the eighth day needs healing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא says that since מילה was given for the eighth day and it needs healing, רפואה was fixed as the eighth ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא said: since circumcision was given on the eighth day, and it needs healing, they set healing as the eighth blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אחא connects the eighth ברכה to ברית מילה, which happens on the eighth day and requires healing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The link is the number eight. מילה is on day eight, and a baby after מילה needs to heal. So the ברכה for healing was given the eighth slot.

phrases.english: Rabbi Acha said:
Since circumcision was given for the eighth [day]
which needs healing,
therefore they fixed it as the eighth [blessing].

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁנִּתְּנָה מִילָה בִּשְׁמִינִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רפואה is eighth because מילה is on the eighth day and needs healing.

steps.title: Why is the blessing of the years ninth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ברכת השנים, the ברכה for a good year of produce, is ninth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did they choose to put the blessing of the years ninth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the next ברכה, the one for rain and good crops, and why it is ninth. The answer follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same pattern continues, this time with the number nine. The answer will need something connected to nine.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing of the years, 'ברך עלינו', asking for rain and good produce

phrases.english: And what did they see to say
the blessing of the years as the ninth?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה רָאוּ לוֹמַר בִּרְכַּת הַשָּׁנִים בִּתְשִׁיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same question pattern, applied to the ninth ברכה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason ברכת השנים is the ninth ברכה.

steps.title: רבי אלכסנדרי: against price gougers, from the ninth psalm
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלכסנדרי says ברכת השנים opposes those who drive up food prices. דוד asked 'break the arm of the wicked' in the ninth chapter of תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלכסנדרי said: it is against those who raise prices, as it says 'Break the arm of the wicked,' and when דוד said it, he said it in the ninth psalm.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלכסנדרי explains that this ברכה is aimed against those who drive up food prices. דוד's prayer against such wicked people appears in the ninth chapter of תהלים, which is why the ברכה is ninth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A good harvest makes food plentiful and cheap, which defeats people who exploit shortages. דוד's request 'שבור זרוע רשע' targets them. That request is in what the גמרא counts as the ninth chapter, because chapters 1 and 2 are counted as one, so our chapter 10 is the ninth.

keyTerms.meaning: Break the arm of the wicked (תהלים י:טו)

steps.confusionAlert: In our printed תהלים this פסוק is in chapter 10. The גמרא calls it the ninth because chapters 1 and 2 are counted as one chapter.

phrases.english: Rabbi Alexandri said:
It corresponds to those who raise prices,
as it is written: 'Break the arm of the wicked,'
and when David said it,
he said it in the ninth [psalm].

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲלֶכְּסַנְדְּרִי: כְּנֶגֶד מַפְקִיעֵי שְׁעָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ברכת השנים is ninth because it opposes price gougers, and דוד's prayer against them is in the ninth psalm.

steps.title: Why does ingathering of exiles follow the blessing of the years?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why קיבוץ גליות comes right after ברכת השנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did they choose to put the ingathering of the exiles after the blessing of the years?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about the order between two ברכות: why gathering the exiles comes right after the ברכה for good crops. The answer is in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Notice the shift in the question. It is no longer 'why number ten' but 'why after the previous ברכה.' So the answer will show that one event follows the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Ingathering of the exiles, the ברכה 'תקע בשופר'

phrases.english: And what did they see to say the ingathering of exiles
after the blessing of the years?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה רָאוּ לוֹמַר קִיבּוּץ גָּלִיּוֹת לְאַחַר בִּרְכַּת הַשָּׁנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same question pattern, now asking about sequence rather than number.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why קיבוץ גליות directly follows ברכת השנים.

steps.title: יחזקאל: the land gives fruit, then the people return
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in יחזקאל says the mountains of Israel will produce fruit for the people who are about to come, so the ingathering follows the land's blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And you, mountains of Israel, give your branches and bear your fruit for My people Israel, for they are about to come.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק showing that first the land becomes fruitful and then the exiles come home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has the land producing fruit 'because they are about to come.' A flourishing land is the step right before the return. That is the same order as ברכת השנים followed by קיבוץ גליות.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And you, mountains of Israel,'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל לו:ח

phrases.english: you shall give your branches
and bear your fruit for My people Israel,
for they are about to come.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 36 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Per יחזקאל, the land blooms first and then the exiles arrive, so קיבוץ גליות follows ברכת השנים.

steps.title: After the ingathering comes judgment and restored judges
steps.stepSummary: Once the exiles are gathered, judgment is carried out on the wicked. Two פסוקים in ישעיה show this, which is why 'השיבה שופטינו' follows קיבוץ גליות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And once the exiles are gathered, judgment is done to the wicked, as it says 'I will turn My hand against you and purge your dross as with lye,' and it is written 'I will restore your judges as at first.'
steps.whatsHappening: Without asking a new question, the גמרא continues the sequence. After the exiles are gathered, the wicked are judged and the judges are restored. This explains why the ברכה 'השיבה שופטינו' comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק describes ה׳ cleaning away the impurities, meaning removing the wicked. The very next פסוק speaks of restoring the judges. Together they show that justice and proper judges follow the ingathering, matching the order of the ברכות.

keyTerms.meaning: Judgment is carried out on the wicked
I will purge your dross as with lye
I will restore your judges, the basis of 'השיבה שופטינו'

steps.whatToRemember: The middle ברכות follow a sequence: good harvest, then gathering the exiles, then judgment on the wicked and restored judges.

phrases.english: And once the exiles have been gathered,
judgment is carried out on the wicked,
as it is said: 'And I will turn My hand against you'
phrases.notes: ישעיה א:כה

phrases.english: 'and purge away your dross as with lye,'
and it is written: 'And I will restore your judges as at first.'
phrases.notes: ישעיה א:כו, the very next פסוק

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן שֶׁנִּתְקַבְּצוּ גָּלִיּוֹת נַעֲשֶׂה דִּין בָּרְשָׁעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the chain from קיבוץ גליות to the next ברכה, השיבה שופטינו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After קיבוץ גליות comes judgment on the wicked and restored judges, so 'השיבה שופטינו' follows 'תקע בשופר'.

steps.title: Why the blessing against heretics follows the blessing of judges
steps.stepSummary: Once judgment is done to the wicked, the heretics come to an end, and evildoers are included with them. This is why ברכת המינים comes after השיבה שופטינו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And once judgment is carried out on the wicked, the heretics come to an end. And we include the evildoers together with them, as it says: 'And the destruction of the transgressors and the sinners will be together, (they will come to an end).'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why ברכת המינים, the ברכה against heretics, comes right after the ברכה about restoring judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 38 said that after the exiles are gathered, judgment comes on the wicked. Here the גמרא adds the next stage: real justice makes the heretics disappear. The פסוק in ישעיה joins פושעים and חטאים together, so the same ברכה also covers the זדים, the evildoers.

keyTerms.meaning: they came to an end, they were wiped out
transgressors. Here it means heretics, the מִינִים
includes, adds into the same ברכה

steps.confusionAlert: The word פושעים here does not just mean ordinary sinners. It refers to heretics, the subject of ברכת המינים. The word 'יכלו' comes from the end of the פסוק, which is why it appears in parentheses.

phrases.english: And once judgment is carried out on the wicked
phrases.notes: This picks up from step 38, the ברכה of השיבה שופטינו.

phrases.english: the transgressors (heretics) come to an end,
phrases.notes: This is the theme of ברכת המינים.

phrases.english: and one includes the evildoers with them,
phrases.notes: The ברכה also mentions זדים.

phrases.english: as it says: 'And the destruction of transgressors and sinners together, (they will cease).'
phrases.notes: ישעיה 1:28

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the chain of ברכות by moving from the judges ברכה to ברכת המינים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכת המינים follows השיבה שופטינו, because once judgment is done, the heretics and evildoers are destroyed together.

steps.title: Why the blessing of the righteous follows the blessing against heretics
steps.stepSummary: Once the heretics are gone, the 'horn' (honor) of the righteous is raised, as the פסוק in תהלים says. So ברכת הצדיקים comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: And once the heretics are gone, the horn of the righteous is raised, as it is written: 'And all the horns of the wicked I will cut off; the horns of the righteous will be raised.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברכה for the righteous, על הצדיקים, comes right after ברכת המינים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק has both halves: the wicked are cut down, and then the righteous are raised. That two-part order in the פסוק is the order of the two ברכות in תפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: horn. A picture of strength and honor
the righteous, the theme of ברכת על הצדיקים

phrases.english: And once the heretics are gone
phrases.notes: This links back to ברכת המינים.

phrases.english: the horn of the righteous is raised,
phrases.notes: This is the theme of the next ברכה.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'And all the horns of the wicked I will cut off,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 75:11

phrases.english: 'the horns of the righteous will be raised.'
phrases.notes: Notice the order inside the פסוק: first the wicked fall, then the righteous rise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the result of step 39 (the heretics are gone) and builds the next ברכה on it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: על הצדיקים follows ברכת המינים, because after the wicked are cut down, the righteous are raised.

steps.title: Righteous converts are included with the righteous
steps.stepSummary: The ברכה of the righteous also mentions גירי הצדק. The proof is that in ויקרא, honoring the elder is placed right next to the מצוה about the convert.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one includes the righteous converts with the righteous, as it says: 'Before the gray-haired you shall rise, and honor the face of the elder,' and right next to it: 'And if a convert lives with you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why converts are mentioned inside the same ברכה as the righteous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The זקן in the פסוק is understood as a Torah scholar, one of the righteous. The very next פסוק is about the גר. Because the two פסוקים sit side by side (a סמיכות), the convert is placed alongside the righteous in תפילה too.

keyTerms.meaning: righteous converts, sincere converts to Judaism
elder. Here it means a Torah scholar
and right next to it. A proof from two פסוקים placed side by side

steps.confusionAlert: The proof does not come from the words of one פסוק. It comes from the placement of two פסוקים next to each other: the elder in ויקרא 19:32 and the convert in 19:33.

phrases.english: And one includes the righteous converts with the righteous,
phrases.notes: The ברכה says 'ועל גרי הצדק'.

phrases.english: as it says: 'Before the gray-haired you shall rise,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:32

phrases.english: 'and honor the face of the elder,'
phrases.notes: זקן is read as a Torah scholar, someone righteous.

phrases.english: and right next to it: 'And if a convert lives with you.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:33. The placement next to the elder links the convert to the righteous.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail to the ברכה from step 40: who else is included in it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Righteous converts are mentioned in ברכת הצדיקים, based on the side-by-side placement of the elder and the convert in ויקרא.

steps.title: The righteous are raised in ירושלים, so rebuilding ירושלים comes next
steps.stepSummary: The righteous are raised up in ירושלים, as the פסוק says 'those who love you will have peace.' So the ברכה of בונה ירושלים follows ברכת הצדיקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where is their horn raised? In ירושלים, as it says: 'Ask for the peace of ירושלים; those who love you will be at peace.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks and answers its own question to explain why the ברכה of rebuilding ירושלים comes after the ברכה of the righteous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question 'where?' is not a real challenge. It is a way to link the two ברכות. 'Those who love you,' meaning those who love ירושלים, are the righteous, and they prosper in ירושלים. So after praying for the righteous, we pray for ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: they will be at peace, they will prosper
those who love you (ירושלים). Understood as the righteous

phrases.english: And where is their horn raised? In Jerusalem,
phrases.notes: The גמרא asks and answers in one breath to connect the two ברכות.

phrases.english: as it says: 'Ask for the peace of Jerusalem;'
phrases.notes: תהלים 122:6

phrases.english: 'those who love you will be at peace.'
phrases.notes: Those who love ירושלים are the righteous, and their success is tied to ירושלים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a quick question-and-answer to move from ברכת הצדיקים to בונה ירושלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בונה ירושלים follows ברכת הצדיקים, because the righteous are raised up in ירושלים.

steps.title: Once ירושלים is rebuilt, דוד comes
steps.stepSummary: After ירושלים is rebuilt, משיח בן דוד comes. This explains why את צמח דוד follows בונה ירושלים. The proof פסוק begins on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And once ירושלים is rebuilt, דוד comes, as it says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the reason for the next ברכה, את צמח דוד: after ירושלים is rebuilt, the king from דוד's family comes. The פסוק that proves it comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'דוד' here means משיח, the descendant of דוד. The chain keeps moving forward: ירושלים is rebuilt first, and then the kingship of דוד returns. The source is still incomplete here, so the learner should expect the פסוק next.

keyTerms.meaning: David comes, meaning משיח בן דוד

steps.whatToRemember: The ברכות follow a sequence of redemption: the exiles are gathered, then the judges return, the heretics are destroyed, the righteous rise, ירושלים is rebuilt, and then משיח בן דוד comes.

phrases.english: And once Jerusalem is rebuilt
phrases.notes: This links back to the ברכה of בונה ירושלים.

phrases.english: David (the Messiah) comes, as it says:
phrases.notes: The פסוק continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from בונה ירושלים to the next ברכה, about the kingship of דוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: את צמח דוד follows בונה ירושלים, because משיח בן דוד comes after ירושלים is rebuilt (the פסוק follows on the next amud).
